overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Fried Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Ma’liya)
recipes.titleEn: Fried Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Ma’liya)

uniqueInstructions.text: Blanch the meat and drain it (head meat is always sold boned).
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Blanch the meat and drain it (head meat is always sold boned).

uniqueInstructions.text: Return it to the pot with the chopped onion, peppercorns, salt and just enough water to cover, and cook until tender.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Return it to the pot with the chopped onion, peppercorns, salt and just enough water to cover, and cook until tender.

uniqueInstructions.text: Drain the meat and fry it in the oil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drain the meat and fry it in the oil.

uniqueInstructions.text: Strain the stock, thicken it with the cornflour and serve it in a separate bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Strain the stock, thicken it with the cornflour and serve it in a separate bowl.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Braised Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Matbukha)
recipes.titleEn: Braised Beef Head Meat (Lahmit al-Ras Matbukha)

uniqueInstructions.text: Rub the onion with salt, pepper and mixed spice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Rub the onion with salt, pepper and mixed spice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put it in a pot with the meat and oil and cook over a very low heat until the meat has reabsorbed the juices it releases.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put it in a pot with the meat and oil and cook over a very low heat until the meat has reabsorbed the juices it releases.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add a little water, and more whenever it dries out, and cook until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add a little water, and more whenever it dries out, and cook until the meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

masterIngredients.name: Egg (whole, with its crushed shell, to clear the stock)
masterIngredients.nameEn: Egg (whole, with its crushed shell, to clear the stock)

uniqueInstructions.text: Have the skull split lengthwise. Soak it in several changes of salted water, singe off any hairs and scrape it with a blunt knife, then wash under running water and blanch.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Have the skull split lengthwise. Soak it in several changes of salted water, singe off any hairs and scrape it with a blunt knife, then wash under running water and blanch.

uniqueInstructions.text: Remove the brain and keep it for another dish.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Remove the brain and keep it for another dish.

uniqueInstructions.text: Simmer the head over a very low heat for 2–3 hours with the onion, carrot, celery, cardamom, bay leaf, peppercorns, lemon rind and the whole egg (yolk, white and crushed shell).
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Simmer the head over a very low heat for 2–3 hours with the onion, carrot, celery, cardamom, bay leaf, peppercorns, lemon rind and the whole egg (yolk, white and crushed shell).

uniqueInstructions.text: Strain the stock, season it and set aside.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Strain the stock, season it and set aside.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the meat and tongue into small, even pieces.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the meat and tongue into small, even pieces.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook the peas and diced carrots in salted water until soft, drain, cool and mix with the chopped pickles.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook the peas and diced carrots in salted water until soft, drain, cool and mix with the chopped pickles.

uniqueInstructions.text: Line the bottom of a cake mould with meat, cover with the vegetables and finish with another layer of meat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Line the bottom of a cake mould with meat, cover with the vegetables and finish with another layer of meat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour the stock over and leave to cool. When the jelly has set, turn it out onto a serving dish.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour the stock over and leave to cool. When the jelly has set, turn it out onto a serving dish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

masterIngredients.name: Garlic cloves, peeled and halved diagonally
masterIngredients.nameEn: Garlic cloves, peeled and halved diagonally

uniqueInstructions.text: Slice the heart and soak it in salted water for 1–2 hours. Rinse in several changes of water, gently squeezing out the blood.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Slice the heart and soak it in salted water for 1–2 hours. Rinse in several changes of water, gently squeezing out the blood.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook the slices over a low heat, stirring often, until they give up their juice, then drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook the slices over a low heat, stirring often, until they give up their juice, then drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the heart and garlic lightly in the oil and season.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the heart and garlic lightly in the oil and season.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover with meat stock and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover with meat stock and simmer for 30–40 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: In tomato sauce (recipe 197 in the book): use 2–3 cups of tomato sauce instead of the stock.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: In tomato sauce (recipe 197 in the book): use 2–3 cups of tomato sauce instead of the stock.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

uniqueInstructions.text: Remove the skin and fat from the kidneys, cut them into walnut-sized pieces and soak in several changes of salted water for at least an hour. Drain and pat dry.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Remove the skin and fat from the kidneys, cut them into walnut-sized pieces and soak in several changes of salted water for at least an hour. Drain and pat dry.

uniqueInstructions.text: Sauté the onions in oil, add the kidneys and fry, stirring now and then, until their juices are absorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sauté the onions in oil, add the kidneys and fry, stirring now and then, until their juices are absorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the stock with salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the stock with salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Lift the kidneys onto a warm dish.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Lift the kidneys onto a warm dish.

uniqueInstructions.text: Thicken the pan juices with the cornflour, add the nutmeg, check the seasoning and pour over the kidneys.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Thicken the pan juices with the cornflour, add the nutmeg, check the seasoning and pour over the kidneys.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Mujaddara (Brown Lentils and Rice with Fried Onions)
recipes.titleEn: Mujaddara (Brown Lentils and Rice with Fried Onions)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover the lentils with twice their volume of water and boil until almost done.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover the lentils with twice their volume of water and boil until almost done.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the rice and salt, stir, cover and cook for about 15 minutes, until both lentils and rice are tender.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the rice and salt, stir, cover and cook for about 15 minutes, until both lentils and rice are tender.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onions until deep brown.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onions until deep brown.

uniqueInstructions.text: Tip the onions and their oil into the lentils, stir and simmer for 5 minutes more.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Tip the onions and their oil into the lentils, stir and simmer for 5 minutes more.

uniqueInstructions.text: Serve hot or cold. It should be soft, like a thick porridge.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Serve hot or cold. It should be soft, like a thick porridge.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Palestinian dish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Turkish Fried Liver with Spring Onion and Parsley (Ciğer Tava)
recipes.titleEn: Turkish Fried Liver with Spring Onion and Parsley (Ciğer Tava)

uniqueInstructions.text: Soak the liver in salted water for 30 minutes, drain, pat dry and cut into 3 cm cubes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soak the liver in salted water for 30 minutes, drain, pat dry and cut into 3 cm cubes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Coat the cubes in seasoned flour and fry until nicely browned, taking care not to overcook them.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Coat the cubes in seasoned flour and fry until nicely browned, taking care not to overcook them.

uniqueInstructions.text: Season, scatter over the spring onions and parsley and toss together.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Season, scatter over the spring onions and parsley and toss together.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Turkish dish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Yemeni Liver and Kidney Stew (Kirsheh)

uniqueInstructions.text: Wash and skin the kidney, chop it coarsely and soak in several changes of water. Drain and pat dry. Cut the liver into small cubes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Wash and skin the kidney, chop it coarsely and soak in several changes of water. Drain and pat dry. Cut the liver into small cubes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pound the garlic with the turmeric, cumin, coriander and cardamom into a thick paste.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pound the garlic with the turmeric, cumin, coriander and cardamom into a thick paste.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the kidney in oil, stirring, until its juices have been absorbed or evaporated, then lift it out.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the kidney in oil, stirring, until its juices have been absorbed or evaporated, then lift it out.

uniqueInstructions.text: Soften the onions in the same oil, lower the heat right down, add the ginger and garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soften the onions in the same oil, lower the heat right down, add the ginger and garlic paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.

uniqueInstructions.text: Return the kidney, turn up the heat, add the liver and cook for 7–10 minutes, still stirring.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Return the kidney, turn up the heat, add the liver and cook for 7–10 minutes, still stirring.

uniqueInstructions.text: When the liver is browned, add the tomatoes with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are done.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: When the liver is browned, add the tomatoes with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are done.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Yemeni dish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Beef with Garlic and Coriander (Kuzbariyit al-Lahma)
recipes.titleEn: Beef with Garlic and Coriander (Kuzbariyit al-Lahma)

uniqueInstructions.text: Crush the garlic with salt and mix it with the coriander.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Crush the garlic with salt and mix it with the coriander.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the beef into small cubes and fry in the oil until it has reabsorbed its juices.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the beef into small cubes and fry in the oil until it has reabsorbed its juices.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the garlic mixture in a separate pan and add it to the beef.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the garlic mixture in a separate pan and add it to the beef.

uniqueInstructions.text: Season, cover the meat with stock or water and simmer gently for 60–90 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Season, cover the meat with stock or water and simmer gently for 60–90 minutes.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Pressed Beef with Onion and Tomato Gravy (Kanduza)
recipes.titleEn: Pressed Beef with Onion and Tomato Gravy (Kanduza)

uniqueInstructions.text: Slice the beef 2 cm thick and pound to tenderise.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Slice the beef 2 cm thick and pound to tenderise.

uniqueInstructions.text: Layer onions, beef and tomatoes in a pot, seasoning each layer lightly.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Layer onions, beef and tomatoes in a pot, seasoning each layer lightly.

uniqueInstructions.text: Weigh the layers down, add 1 cup of water and cook over a low heat for 30–40 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Weigh the layers down, add 1 cup of water and cook over a low heat for 30–40 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Take out the beef, fry it in oil and keep it warm on a serving dish.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Take out the beef, fry it in oil and keep it warm on a serving dish.

uniqueInstructions.text: Blend the vegetables with their juices, strain, and return to the pot.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Blend the vegetables with their juices, strain, and return to the pot.

uniqueInstructions.text: Season, stir in the cornflour, cook for 2–3 minutes and pour over the beef.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Season, stir in the cornflour, cook for 2–3 minutes and pour over the beef.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pierce the meat in several places with the tip of a sharp knife.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pierce the meat in several places with the tip of a sharp knife.

uniqueInstructions.text: Roll each garlic clove in salt and pepper and push it into one of the holes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Roll each garlic clove in salt and pepper and push it into one of the holes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Brown the meat all over in hot oil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Brown the meat all over in hot oil.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add water to come halfway up the meat and cook until tender.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add water to come halfway up the meat and cook until tender.

uniqueInstructions.text: Chill before slicing.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Chill before slicing.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Cheese and Parsley Beef Rolls in Onion Gravy (Lahma Mahshiya)
recipes.titleEn: Cheese and Parsley Beef Rolls in Onion Gravy (Lahma Mahshiya)

uniqueInstructions.text: Slice the beef very thinly, cut it into 10 cm squares and pound to tenderise.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Slice the beef very thinly, cut it into 10 cm squares and pound to tenderise.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix the cheeses with the parsley, spread a little on each slice, roll it up and tie with thread.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix the cheeses with the parsley, spread a little on each slice, roll it up and tie with thread.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put the rolls in a glass or ceramic dish, pour over the blended marinade ingredients and leave for 1–2 hours.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put the rolls in a glass or ceramic dish, pour over the blended marinade ingredients and leave for 1–2 hours.

uniqueInstructions.text: Brush off the marinade (keep it), brown the rolls lightly and arrange them in a baking pan.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Brush off the marinade (keep it), brown the rolls lightly and arrange them in a baking pan.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the flour in a little oil, take it off the heat and gradually whisk in the strained marinade. Cook for 3–5 minutes and pour over the rolls, adding warm water if the meat is not covered.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the flour in a little oil, take it off the heat and gradually whisk in the strained marinade. Cook for 3–5 minutes and pour over the rolls, adding warm water if the meat is not covered.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes. Snip off the threads before serving.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes. Snip off the threads before serving.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Fried Beef and Egg Patties (Kufta bi-l-Beid)
recipes.titleEn: Fried Beef and Egg Patties (Kufta bi-l-Beid)

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the beef, onion and breadcrumbs together twice, or pound them until smooth.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the beef, onion and breadcrumbs together twice, or pound them until smooth.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and work them into the meat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and work them into the meat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Shape into round patties 5–7 cm across and 2 cm thick.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Shape into round patties 5–7 cm across and 2 cm thick.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry in oil until browned on both sides and cooked through.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry in oil until browned on both sides and cooked through.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Garlic Meatballs in Sweet-Sour Tomato Sauce (Kufta bi-l-Toom wi-l-Bassal)
recipes.titleEn: Garlic Meatballs in Sweet-Sour Tomato Sauce (Kufta bi-l-Toom wi-l-Bassal)

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the beef, onion and garlic together twice, or pound until smooth. Season and mix.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the beef, onion and garlic together twice, or pound until smooth. Season and mix.

uniqueInstructions.text: Shape into small balls and fry.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Shape into small balls and fry.

uniqueInstructions.text: Dissolve the vinegar and sugar in the tomato juice and cook for 3–5 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Dissolve the vinegar and sugar in the tomato juice and cook for 3–5 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently now and then so they do not stick.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently now and then so they do not stick.

uniqueInstructions.text: Thicken the sauce with the cornflour.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Thicken the sauce with the cornflour.

recipes.title: Leek Meatballs in Lemon Broth (Kufta bi-l-Kurrat)
recipes.titleEn: Leek Meatballs in Lemon Broth (Kufta bi-l-Kurrat)

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil the leeks in salted water until tender and drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil the leeks in salted water until tender and drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the beef and leeks together twice, then mix in the beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the beef and leeks together twice, then mix in the beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Shape into small balls and fry.

uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bring 2 cups of water to the boil with 1 tablespoon of oil and the lemon juice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Slip in the meatballs and simmer for about 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently so they do not stick.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Slip in the meatballs and simmer for about 30 minutes, shaking the pot gently so they do not stick.

recipes.titleEn: Lamb Stew with Crisp Potato Fingers (Lahma Dani Matbukha)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel the tomato, garlic and onion.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel the tomato, garlic and onion.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook the meat with the whole vegetables in oil over a very low heat until the juices have been reabsorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook the meat with the whole vegetables in oil over a very low heat until the juices have been reabsorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour, until tender.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour, until tender.

uniqueInstructions.text: Lift the meat onto a serving dish and keep warm.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Lift the meat onto a serving dish and keep warm.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mash the vegetables into the broth until smooth, bring it to the boil and toss in the fried potatoes. Cook for 3–5 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mash the vegetables into the broth until smooth, bring it to the boil and toss in the fried potatoes. Cook for 3–5 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour over the meat and serve hot.

recipes.title: Braised Veal Shin with Straw Potatoes (Moza Matbukha)
recipes.titleEn: Braised Veal Shin with Straw Potatoes (Moza Matbukha)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes and slice the onions coarsely.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes and slice the onions coarsely.

uniqueInstructions.text: Sauté the onions in oil, add the meat and brown it all over.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sauté the onions in oil, add the meat and brown it all over.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover with warm water, season and cook over a very low heat for about an hour.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the peeled potatoes into matchsticks, fry until very crisp and drain on absorbent paper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the peeled potatoes into matchsticks, fry until very crisp and drain on absorbent paper.

uniqueInstructions.text: When the meat is ready, add the potatoes and cook for about 10 minutes so they soak up the juices.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: When the meat is ready, add the potatoes and cook for about 10 minutes so they soak up the juices.

recipes.title: Tunisian Lamb and Parsley Tajine (Tajine Ma’doones)
recipes.titleEn: Tunisian Lamb and Parsley Tajine (Tajine Ma’doones)

uniqueInstructions.text: Soak the beans overnight, then boil them in fresh water for 20–30 minutes. Drain, keeping the liquid.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soak the beans overnight, then boil them in fresh water for 20–30 minutes. Drain, keeping the liquid.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and roll them in salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and roll them in salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Soften the onions in olive oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices have been reabsorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soften the onions in olive oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices have been reabsorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the cayenne, beans, tabil and the tomato paste dissolved in enough bean liquid to just cover the lamb. Cook until the lamb and beans are tender, then take off the heat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the cayenne, beans, tabil and the tomato paste dissolved in enough bean liquid to just cover the lamb. Cook until the lamb and beans are tender, then take off the heat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat the eggs with the parsley, breadcrumbs, cheese and seasoning and stir them thoroughly into the lamb.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat the eggs with the parsley, breadcrumbs, cheese and seasoning and stir them thoroughly into the lamb.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour into a well-greased ovenproof dish and bake in a moderate oven for 15–20 minutes, until set.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour into a well-greased ovenproof dish and bake in a moderate oven for 15–20 minutes, until set.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Tunisian tajine: unlike the Moroccan stew, it is baked with eggs until firm, like a thick frittata.

recipes.title: Tunisian Lamb and Mint Tajine (Tajine Na‘na‘)
recipes.titleEn: Tunisian Lamb and Mint Tajine (Tajine Na‘na‘)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the lamb into bite-sized pieces and roll them in salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the lamb into bite-sized pieces and roll them in salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onions in ghee until golden, add the lamb and brown it until its juices are reabsorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onions in ghee until golden, add the lamb and brown it until its juices are reabsorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Stir in the tomatoes, tabil and seasoning and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes, adding hot water if the meat is not covered.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Stir in the tomatoes, tabil and seasoning and cook over a low heat for 30 minutes, adding hot water if the meat is not covered.

uniqueInstructions.text: Drain the meat, keeping the broth, and put it in a greased casserole.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drain the meat, keeping the broth, and put it in a greased casserole.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat the eggs with the cheese, mint, breadcrumbs and seasoning, mix in the meat and 1 cup of the broth, and pour back into the casserole.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat the eggs with the cheese, mint, breadcrumbs and seasoning, mix in the meat and 1 cup of the broth, and pour back into the casserole.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in a moderate oven for 20 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in a moderate oven for 20 minutes.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Tunisian dish.

recipes.title: Cypriot Tava (Lamb and Tomato Slow-Baked with Cumin)
recipes.titleEn: Cypriot Tava (Lamb and Tomato Slow-Baked with Cumin)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Thin the tomato paste with 1/2 cup of warm water and put it in a casserole with all the other ingredients.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Thin the tomato paste with 1/2 cup of warm water and put it in a casserole with all the other ingredients.

uniqueInstructions.text: Close with a tight-fitting lid and bake in a moderate oven for 2–3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Close with a tight-fitting lid and bake in a moderate oven for 2–3 hours, until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Cypriot dish named after the tava, the unglazed terracotta pot with a tight lid it is always cooked in.

recipes.title: Tunisian Lamb and Potato Meatballs (Kabaar)

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil the potatoes until very soft, then peel and mash them.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil the potatoes until very soft, then peel and mash them.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the lamb twice with the onions, garlic, parsley, coriander, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the lamb twice with the onions, garlic, parsley, coriander, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix in the mashed potato, breadcrumbs, cinnamon and well-beaten eggs.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix in the mashed potato, breadcrumbs, cinnamon and well-beaten eggs.

uniqueInstructions.text: Shape into small balls and chill for 30 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Shape into small balls and chill for 30 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry in very hot oil until browned all over.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry in very hot oil until browned all over.

recipes.title: Baked Kofta Rolls with Pine Nuts (Kafta Mabroomeh / Mkabtaleh)
recipes.titleEn: Baked Kofta Rolls with Pine Nuts (Kafta Mabroomeh / Mkabtaleh)

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the meat twice with the onions, garlic, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the meat twice with the onions, garlic, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat the eggs, add them to the meat and knead well.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat the eggs, add them to the meat and knead well.

uniqueInstructions.text: Roll the meat out about 1 cm thick on a lightly greased surface and cut it into rounds.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Roll the meat out about 1 cm thick on a lightly greased surface and cut it into rounds.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put a few pine nuts in the middle of each round and roll it up.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put a few pine nuts in the middle of each round and roll it up.

uniqueInstructions.text: Arrange the rolls on a well-greased tray and brush each with fat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Arrange the rolls on a well-greased tray and brush each with fat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in the middle of a moderate oven for 30 minutes, then brown under the grill, shaking the tray so they colour evenly.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in the middle of a moderate oven for 30 minutes, then brown under the grill, shaking the tray so they colour evenly.

recipes.culturalNotes: Called kafta mabroomeh in Syria and kafta mkabtaleh in Lebanon; only the name differs.

recipes.title: Lebanese Kafta Fatteh with Garlic Yogurt (Fatteet Kafta Madqooqa)
recipes.titleEn: Lebanese Kafta Fatteh with Garlic Yogurt (Fatteet Kafta Madqooqa)

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the lamb twice with the fresh mint, salt and pepper, and shape into patties.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the lamb twice with the fresh mint, salt and pepper, and shape into patties.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the patties until nicely browned.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the patties until nicely browned.

uniqueInstructions.text: Break the bread into bite-sized pieces and put them in a deep serving bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Break the bread into bite-sized pieces and put them in a deep serving bowl.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix the yogurt with the garlic and dried mint, then stir in the oil left from frying the patties.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix the yogurt with the garlic and dried mint, then stir in the oil left from frying the patties.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour the yogurt over the bread and top with the kafta.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour the yogurt over the bread and top with the kafta.

recipes.title: Izmir Meatballs in Tomato Sauce (İzmir Köftesi)
recipes.titleEn: Izmir Meatballs in Tomato Sauce (İzmir Köftesi)

masterIngredients.name: Sauce: sweet green pepper, very finely diced
masterIngredients.nameEn: Sauce: sweet green pepper, very finely diced

uniqueInstructions.text: Sprinkle the bread with cold water and squeeze it out.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sprinkle the bread with cold water and squeeze it out.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mince the bread twice with the beef, onions, parsley, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper, then knead in the egg.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mince the bread twice with the beef, onions, parsley, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper, then knead in the egg.

uniqueInstructions.text: With wet hands, shape round or oval balls and roll them very lightly in seasoned flour.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: With wet hands, shape round or oval balls and roll them very lightly in seasoned flour.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the meatballs lightly and drain them on absorbent paper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the meatballs lightly and drain them on absorbent paper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Soften the green pepper in the same oil, add the tomato juice, sugar, salt and pepper and cook for 10–12 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soften the green pepper in the same oil, add the tomato juice, sugar, salt and pepper and cook for 10–12 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Return the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Return the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

recipes.title: Upper Egyptian Mashed Okra with Beef and Chili (Bamya Weeka Sa‘idi)
recipes.titleEn: Upper Egyptian Mashed Okra with Beef and Chili (Bamya Weeka Sa‘idi)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the beef into small cubes and boil it in the stock for 20–30 minutes, until tender. Lift it out.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the beef into small cubes and boil it in the stock for 20–30 minutes, until tender. Lift it out.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the okra and chilies to the broth, cook for about 10 minutes, then mash with a fork.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the okra and chilies to the broth, cook for about 10 minutes, then mash with a fork.

uniqueInstructions.text: Return the meat to the pot.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Return the meat to the pot.

uniqueInstructions.text: Make the ta’liya: pound the garlic with the coriander, salt and pepper and fry it in the oil for 3–5 minutes. Tip it into the pot, swirl a spoonful of broth round the frying pan and add that too.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Make the ta’liya: pound the garlic with the coriander, salt and pepper and fry it in the oil for 3–5 minutes. Tip it into the pot, swirl a spoonful of broth round the frying pan and add that too.

uniqueInstructions.text: Simmer for 5–7 minutes and serve.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Simmer for 5–7 minutes and serve.

recipes.culturalNotes: Weeka is the Upper Egyptian name for okra cooked until it breaks down into a thick, silky stew.

recipes.title: Iraqi Okra Stew with Tamarind (Bamia Marag)
recipes.titleEn: Iraqi Okra Stew with Tamarind (Bamia Marag)

masterIngredients.name: Cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns
masterIngredients.nameEn: Cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the mutton into bite-sized cubes and boil with the spices until tender. Lift it out, keeping the broth.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the mutton into bite-sized cubes and boil with the spices until tender. Lift it out, keeping the broth.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the mutton in ghee, then add the okra and garlic and stir until everything is well fried.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the mutton in ghee, then add the okra and garlic and stir until everything is well fried.

uniqueInstructions.text: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid, season, and add it to the pot with the broth.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid, season, and add it to the pot with the broth.

uniqueInstructions.text: Simmer for 30 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Simmer for 30 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put the onions, still in their skins, in a hot oven for about an hour, until thoroughly cooked.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put the onions, still in their skins, in a hot oven for about an hour, until thoroughly cooked.

uniqueInstructions.text: Peel them at the table; they should be soft enough to melt in the mouth.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Peel them at the table; they should be soft enough to melt in the mouth.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the beef into small cubes. Peel the garlic and halve it diagonally.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the beef into small cubes. Peel the garlic and halve it diagonally.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the beef and onions lightly in oil and move them to a casserole.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the beef and onions lightly in oil and move them to a casserole.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the garlic, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cover with the stock.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the garlic, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cover with the stock.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 90–120 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 90–120 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Thicken the gravy with cornflour if you like.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Thicken the gravy with cornflour if you like.

uniqueInstructions.text: Sweet-sour version (recipe 268 in the book): use 2 cups of tomato juice instead of stock, with 1 teaspoon each of sugar and vinegar dissolved in it, and spice with cinnamon or nutmeg.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sweet-sour version (recipe 268 in the book): use 2 cups of tomato juice instead of stock, with 1 teaspoon each of sugar and vinegar dissolved in it, and spice with cinnamon or nutmeg.

uniqueInstructions.text: Make the savory minced beef: fry the onion in a little oil until pale gold, add the beef, salt and pepper and cook until the juices are absorbed. You need about 1 cup.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Make the savory minced beef: fry the onion in a little oil until pale gold, add the beef, salt and pepper and cook until the juices are absorbed. You need about 1 cup.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the gullash into 10 cm squares and keep them under a cloth so they do not dry out.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the gullash into 10 cm squares and keep them under a cloth so they do not dry out.

uniqueInstructions.text: Working one square at a time, lay a narrow strip of meat across the middle, stopping 1 cm from each end.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Working one square at a time, lay a narrow strip of meat across the middle, stopping 1 cm from each end.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fold in the ends and roll up very tightly.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fold in the ends and roll up very tightly.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pack the fingers into a greased baking pan and brush the tops with melted butter.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pack the fingers into a greased baking pan and brush the tops with melted butter.

recipes.title: Crisp Layered Ruqaq with Cheese and Egg (Saniyit Ru’a’ bi-l-Gibna)
recipes.titleEn: Crisp Layered Ruqaq with Cheese and Egg (Saniyit Ru’a’ bi-l-Gibna)

uniqueInstructions.text: Grate the Balkan cheese. Mash the areesh cheese with the hard-boiled eggs, then mix in the grated cheese, the beaten raw egg and a pinch of pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Grate the Balkan cheese. Mash the areesh cheese with the hard-boiled eggs, then mix in the grated cheese, the beaten raw egg and a pinch of pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Grease a deep baking pan (you will need a second pan the same size). Dip one ruqaq sheet at a time in hot broth and use them to line the pan, sprinkling each layer with a little oil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Grease a deep baking pan (you will need a second pan the same size). Dip one ruqaq sheet at a time in hot broth and use them to line the pan, sprinkling each layer with a little oil.

uniqueInstructions.text: After 3–4 layers, spread the cheese filling evenly, then carry on with more dipped, oiled layers.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: After 3–4 layers, spread the cheese filling evenly, then carry on with more dipped, oiled layers.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour any remaining oil over the top and bake in a moderate oven.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour any remaining oil over the top and bake in a moderate oven.

uniqueInstructions.text: When the top is brown, turn it over into the second pan and return it to the oven to brown the other side.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: When the top is brown, turn it over into the second pan and return it to the oven to brown the other side.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut into pieces while hot.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut into pieces while hot.

recipes.culturalNotes: A cheese version of the meat-filled ruqaq; ruqaq is sold in round packets in Egyptian groceries.

recipes.title: Lamb and Lisan ‘Asfur Pasta Casserole (Tagin Lisan ‘Asfur)
recipes.titleEn: Lamb and Lisan ‘Asfur Pasta Casserole (Tagin Lisan ‘Asfur)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Seed the peppers and slice them thinly.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Seed the peppers and slice them thinly.

uniqueInstructions.text: Sauté the onion in the butter and oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices are absorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sauté the onion in the butter and oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices are absorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover with stock, add the peppers, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook for 15–20 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover with stock, add the peppers, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook for 15–20 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Lift out the meat and vegetables with a slotted spoon and put them in an ovenproof pot.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Lift out the meat and vegetables with a slotted spoon and put them in an ovenproof pot.

uniqueInstructions.text: Parboil the lisan ‘asfur in the stock for 5–7 minutes and pour it over the meat, adding hot water if it is not covered.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Parboil the lisan ‘asfur in the stock for 5–7 minutes and pour it over the meat, adding hot water if it is not covered.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes.

recipes.culturalNotes: Made in Palestine and Lebanon. Lisan ‘asfur, “sparrow’s tongue”, is named for its small oval shape.

recipes.title: Shishbarak (Meat Dumplings in Garlic Yogurt)

uniqueInstructions.text: Sift the flour with salt and add enough water to knead a smooth dough that comes away from the bowl. Rest it for an hour.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sift the flour with salt and add enough water to knead a smooth dough that comes away from the bowl. Rest it for an hour.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the pine nuts golden and set aside. Soften the onion in the same oil, add the meat and fry until its juices are gone, then stir in the pine nuts, spices, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the pine nuts golden and set aside. Soften the onion in the same oil, add the meat and fry until its juices are gone, then stir in the pine nuts, spices, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Roll the dough out on a floured surface and cut it into small rounds.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Roll the dough out on a floured surface and cut it into small rounds.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put 1/2 teaspoon of filling on each, fold into a crescent with wet fingers, then wrap it round your finger and pinch the ends together so it looks like a little hat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put 1/2 teaspoon of filling on each, fold into a crescent with wet fingers, then wrap it round your finger and pinch the ends together so it looks like a little hat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Set them on a greased tray, brush with ghee and bake in a moderate oven until crisp and golden.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Set them on a greased tray, brush with ghee and bake in a moderate oven until crisp and golden.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the garlic in a little ghee until golden, stirring constantly, and stir in the mint.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the garlic in a little ghee until golden, stirring constantly, and stir in the mint.

uniqueInstructions.text: Whisk the egg whites until frothy and mix them into the yogurt to keep it from splitting. Heat it uncovered over a low heat and add the garlic mixture.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Whisk the egg whites until frothy and mix them into the yogurt to keep it from splitting. Heat it uncovered over a low heat and add the garlic mixture.

uniqueInstructions.text: When the yogurt bubbles, add the shishbarak and cook for 7–10 minutes more.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: When the yogurt bubbles, add the shishbarak and cook for 7–10 minutes more.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Palestinian dish, also made across the Levant.

recipes.title: Layered Peas, Rice and Minced Beef Béchamel (Basilla bi-l-Bechamel)
recipes.titleEn: Layered Peas, Rice and Minced Beef Béchamel (Basilla bi-l-Bechamel)

uniqueInstructions.text: Parboil the peas in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Parboil the peas in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Grease a deep ovenproof serving dish, preferably glass.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Grease a deep ovenproof serving dish, preferably glass.

uniqueInstructions.text: Arrange the rice, peas and minced beef in several thin layers, moistening every layer with béchamel.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Arrange the rice, peas and minced beef in several thin layers, moistening every layer with béchamel.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour the beaten egg over the top.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour the beaten egg over the top.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 20–30 minutes, until browned on top.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 20–30 minutes, until browned on top.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Brown Onion Rice for Fish (Ruzz Ahmar)
recipes.titleEn: Brown Onion Rice for Fish (Ruzz Ahmar)

uniqueInstructions.text: Soak the rice in warm water for 15–20 minutes and drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soak the rice in warm water for 15–20 minutes and drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the water and salt and bring to the boil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the water and salt and bring to the boil.

uniqueInstructions.text: Stir in the rice, cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Stir in the rice, cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: For a redder rice (recipe 309 in the book), stir 1 tablespoon of tomato paste into the water before adding the rice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: For a redder rice (recipe 309 in the book), stir 1 tablespoon of tomato paste into the water before adding the rice.

recipes.culturalNotes: In Egypt this rice is always served with fish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Rice Cooked in Shrimp Stock (Ruzz bi-Salsit Gambari)
recipes.titleEn: Rice Cooked in Shrimp Stock (Ruzz bi-Salsit Gambari)

uniqueInstructions.text: Rinse the shrimp under running water until it runs clear. Put them in a pot with the onions, lemons, cumin, salt and pepper, without any water, and cook over a moderate heat, tossing every few minutes, for about 7 minutes or until done.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Rinse the shrimp under running water until it runs clear. Put them in a pot with the onions, lemons, cumin, salt and pepper, without any water, and cook over a moderate heat, tossing every few minutes, for about 7 minutes or until done.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cool and shell the shrimp, keeping the heads, shells and juices. Remove the dark vein.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cool and shell the shrimp, keeping the heads, shells and juices. Remove the dark vein.

uniqueInstructions.text: Make the shrimp sauce: blend the heads, shells and juices at high speed and strain. You need 1 cup.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Make the shrimp sauce: blend the heads, shells and juices at high speed and strain. You need 1 cup.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the rice in the oil, stirring until every grain is coated.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the rice in the oil, stirring until every grain is coated.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add 2 cups of water and the cup of shrimp sauce. It is already well seasoned, so add no salt.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add 2 cups of water and the cup of shrimp sauce. It is already well seasoned, so add no salt.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook uncovered over a moderate heat until the liquid is absorbed, then cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 20–30 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook uncovered over a moderate heat until the liquid is absorbed, then cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 20–30 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Serve with the shrimp.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Serve with the shrimp.

recipes.culturalNotes: The book also suggests the strained shrimp sauce as a flavouring for tahini and other dishes.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Rice with Tomatoes, Peppers and Carrots (Ruzz bi-l-Khudar)
recipes.titleEn: Rice with Tomatoes, Peppers and Carrots (Ruzz bi-l-Khudar)

masterIngredients.name: Sweet green peppers, blanched and thinly sliced
masterIngredients.nameEn: Sweet green peppers, blanched and thinly sliced

uniqueInstructions.text: Sauté the onion until golden and mix it with the tomatoes, peppers and carrots.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sauté the onion until golden and mix it with the tomatoes, peppers and carrots.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the rice in the same oil, stirring, until every grain is coated.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the rice in the same oil, stirring, until every grain is coated.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the vegetables, water, salt and pepper and stir one last time.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the vegetables, water, salt and pepper and stir one last time.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook uncovered over a high heat until the water is absorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook uncovered over a high heat until the water is absorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Soft Rice Porridge with Beef (Ruzz Lubba bi-l-Lahma)
recipes.titleEn: Soft Rice Porridge with Beef (Ruzz Lubba bi-l-Lahma)

uniqueInstructions.text: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onions until golden, add the beef and fry over a high heat until its juices are absorbed.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onions until golden, add the beef and fry over a high heat until its juices are absorbed.

uniqueInstructions.text: Season, add water to cover and cook over a low heat for 15–20 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Season, add water to cover and cook over a low heat for 15–20 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Top up the water to 4–5 cups, stir in the rice and check the seasoning.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Top up the water to 4–5 cups, stir in the rice and check the seasoning.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cover and cook slowly for about 30 minutes. It should end up soft and porridge-like.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cover and cook slowly for about 30 minutes. It should end up soft and porridge-like.

uniqueInstructions.text: With gizzards (recipe 314 in the book): stir 5–6 mastic grains into hot oil for 10–15 seconds, add halved boiled gizzards, cover and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry them, add 4 cups of water and the rice and cook the same way.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: With gizzards (recipe 314 in the book): stir 5–6 mastic grains into hot oil for 10–15 seconds, add halved boiled gizzards, cover and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry them, add 4 cups of water and the rice and cook the same way.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Turkish Eggplant Pilaf (Patlıcanlı Pilav)

uniqueInstructions.text: Dice the eggplant without peeling, salt it and leave for an hour. Squeeze out the moisture and pat dry.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Dice the eggplant without peeling, salt it and leave for an hour. Squeeze out the moisture and pat dry.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the eggplant until lightly browned and drain on absorbent paper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the eggplant until lightly browned and drain on absorbent paper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Soften the chopped onion in the same oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, mint, eggplant, salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soften the chopped onion in the same oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, mint, eggplant, salt and pepper and bring to the boil.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the rice and enough water to cover.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the rice and enough water to cover.

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil hard, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil hard, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 30 minutes.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Turkish dish. The book cooks an onion here without listing it; we added one.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Saffron Rice Kibbeh (Kubbat Halab)

masterIngredients.name: Celery or parsley, very finely chopped
masterIngredients.nameEn: Celery or parsley, very finely chopped

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil the rice in 4 cups of water with the saffron and salt until soft, breaking up any lumps with a fork. Drain off any water left.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil the rice in 4 cups of water with the saffron and salt until soft, breaking up any lumps with a fork. Drain off any water left.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the lightly beaten egg and, with fingers dipped in the turmeric rose water, knead the rice into a soft dough that holds its shape.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the lightly beaten egg and, with fingers dipped in the turmeric rose water, knead the rice into a soft dough that holds its shape.

uniqueInstructions.text: Filling: fry the beef, then add the celery or parsley, almonds, raisins, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cook together over a low heat for 10 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Filling: fry the beef, then add the celery or parsley, almonds, raisins, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cook together over a low heat for 10 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Take a little rice dough in your palm, moistened with rose water, and hollow it out with a finger of the other hand, turning it into a thin cup.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Take a little rice dough in your palm, moistened with rose water, and hollow it out with a finger of the other hand, turning it into a thin cup.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fill with the meat, close it into an oval ball with a moistened palm and set it on a floured surface. Repeat until the dough is used up.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fill with the meat, close it into an oval ball with a moistened palm and set it on a floured surface. Repeat until the dough is used up.

uniqueInstructions.text: Deep-fry in ghee until golden.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Deep-fry in ghee until golden.

recipes.culturalNotes: An Iraqi dish named after Aleppo (Halab).

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Persian Crusty Steamed Rice with Yogurt Tahdig (Chelow Dig)
recipes.titleEn: Persian Crusty Steamed Rice with Yogurt Tahdig (Chelow Dig)

uniqueInstructions.text: Wash the rice in boiling water and drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Wash the rice in boiling water and drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bring 8 cups of heavily salted water to the boil, add the rice, cook for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse in hot water.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bring 8 cups of heavily salted water to the boil, add the rice, cook for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse in hot water.

uniqueInstructions.text: Stir the yogurt into one cup of the half-cooked rice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Stir the yogurt into one cup of the half-cooked rice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Swirl a tablespoon of ghee round the base and sides of a heavy pan and spread the yogurt rice over the bottom.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Swirl a tablespoon of ghee round the base and sides of a heavy pan and spread the yogurt rice over the bottom.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pile the rest of the rice on top, sprinkle with the remaining ghee and steam over a moderate heat, breaking up any clusters, until tender and crusty underneath.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pile the rest of the rice on top, sprinkle with the remaining ghee and steam over a moderate heat, breaking up any clusters, until tender and crusty underneath.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mound the steamed rice in the middle of a dish and break the golden crust from the bottom of the pan into pieces around it.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mound the steamed rice in the middle of a dish and break the golden crust from the bottom of the pan into pieces around it.

recipes.culturalNotes: An Iranian dish; the golden crust is known as tahdig.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Everyday Egyptian Salad Dressing (Khalta li-l-Salata)

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix all the ingredients together.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix all the ingredients together.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour over the salad just before serving.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour over the salad just before serving.

recipes.culturalNotes: The basic dressing the book uses for most of its salads.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Fresh Cabbage Salad with Garlic and Lemon (Salatit Krumb)
recipes.titleEn: Fresh Cabbage Salad with Garlic and Lemon (Salatit Krumb)

uniqueInstructions.text: Sprinkle the cabbage and onion with salt and rub well, then rinse and drain.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sprinkle the cabbage and onion with salt and rub well, then rinse and drain.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and salt.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour over the vegetables and toss.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour over the vegetables and toss.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

masterIngredients.name: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)
masterIngredients.nameEn: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)

uniqueInstructions.text: Only onions and tomatoes are essential; add whatever else the season offers.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Only onions and tomatoes are essential; add whatever else the season offers.

uniqueInstructions.text: Chop everything finely, keeping each vegetable separate.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Chop everything finely, keeping each vegetable separate.

uniqueInstructions.text: Rub the onion with salt, rinse it and leave it to soak in lemon juice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Rub the onion with salt, rinse it and leave it to soak in lemon juice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Rub the inside of the salad bowl with the cut garlic clove and heap the vegetables in it.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Rub the inside of the salad bowl with the cut garlic clove and heap the vegetables in it.

uniqueInstructions.text: Just before serving, add the dressing and toss.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Just before serving, add the dressing and toss.

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

masterIngredients.name: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)
masterIngredients.nameEn: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil the artichoke hearts in salted water until tender, drain and chop.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil the artichoke hearts in salted water until tender, drain and chop.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add them to the chopped eggs.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add them to the chopped eggs.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour over the dressing and mix well.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour over the dressing and mix well.

recipes.title: Green Bean Salad with Red Onion (Salatit Fasulya Khadra)
recipes.titleEn: Green Bean Salad with Red Onion (Salatit Fasulya Khadra)

uniqueInstructions.text: String the beans and trim the tops and tails.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: String the beans and trim the tops and tails.

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil in salted water until tender, drain and spread out to cool.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil in salted water until tender, drain and spread out to cool.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put the sliced onion in the salad bowl to soak in the lemon juice.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put the sliced onion in the salad bowl to soak in the lemon juice.

uniqueInstructions.text: Before serving, add the beans and oil and mix.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Before serving, add the beans and oil and mix.

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Beetroot Salad with Garlic Vinegar (Salatit Bangar bi-l-Toom)
recipes.titleEn: Beetroot Salad with Garlic Vinegar (Salatit Bangar bi-l-Toom)

uniqueInstructions.text: Boil the beetroot for about an hour, until very tender.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Boil the beetroot for about an hour, until very tender.

uniqueInstructions.text: Drain, keeping two tablespoons of the cooking water. Cool, peel and cut into small cubes, thin slices or fingers.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drain, keeping two tablespoons of the cooking water. Cool, peel and cut into small cubes, thin slices or fingers.

uniqueInstructions.text: Crush the garlic with salt until very smooth and mix in the vinegar.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Crush the garlic with salt until very smooth and mix in the vinegar.

uniqueInstructions.text: Stir the garlic dressing into the reserved cooking water, pour over the beetroot and mix gently.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Stir the garlic dressing into the reserved cooking water, pour over the beetroot and mix gently.

uniqueInstructions.text: With tahini (recipe 334 in the book): dress the beetroot with 2 tablespoons of thin tahini sauce instead.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: With tahini (recipe 334 in the book): dress the beetroot with 2 tablespoons of thin tahini sauce instead.

uniqueInstructions.text: With yogurt (recipe 335 in the book): mix the cubed beetroot with 3 diced tomatoes and 3–5 diced cucumbers and cover with 1 cup of garlic yogurt (yogurt, crushed garlic and salt, without mint).
uniqueInstructions.textEn: With yogurt (recipe 335 in the book): mix the cubed beetroot with 3 diced tomatoes and 3–5 diced cucumbers and cover with 1 cup of garlic yogurt (yogurt, crushed garlic and salt, without mint).

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Blanched Cabbage Salad with Salted Fish (Salatit Krumb)
recipes.titleEn: Blanched Cabbage Salad with Salted Fish (Salatit Krumb)

masterIngredients.name: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)
masterIngredients.nameEn: Salad dressing (oil, lemon, vinegar, salt and pepper)

uniqueInstructions.text: Shred the cabbage very finely, blanch it for 1 minute, drain and cool.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Shred the cabbage very finely, blanch it for 1 minute, drain and cool.

uniqueInstructions.text: Chop the fish very finely and stir it into the dressing.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Chop the fish very finely and stir it into the dressing.

uniqueInstructions.text: Pour over the cabbage and mix well.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Pour over the cabbage and mix well.

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Wilted Spinach Salad with Onion and Lemon (Salatit Sabanikh)
recipes.titleEn: Wilted Spinach Salad with Onion and Lemon (Salatit Sabanikh)

uniqueInstructions.text: Chop the spinach leaves and stems coarsely, sprinkle with salt and rub until they lose some juice. Rinse and pat dry.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Chop the spinach leaves and stems coarsely, sprinkle with salt and rub until they lose some juice. Rinse and pat dry.

uniqueInstructions.text: Wilt the spinach over a low heat, drain and spread out to cool.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Wilt the spinach over a low heat, drain and spread out to cool.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix in the onion, lemon juice, oil and salt.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix in the onion, lemon juice, oil and salt.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Turkish Spinach Salad with Feta (Ispanak Salatası)
recipes.titleEn: Turkish Spinach Salad with Feta (Ispanak Salatası)

uniqueInstructions.text: Rinse the spinach, chop it coarsely and wilt it in a pot over the heat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Rinse the spinach, chop it coarsely and wilt it in a pot over the heat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Drain in a colander, pressing with a spoon to squeeze out the moisture, and put it in a bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drain in a colander, pressing with a spoon to squeeze out the moisture, and put it in a bowl.

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onions in the olive oil until golden and add them to the bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onions in the olive oil until golden and add them to the bowl.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the parsley, cheese, salt and pepper and toss well.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the parsley, cheese, salt and pepper and toss well.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Turkish dish.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

uniqueInstructions.text: Melt the butter with the oil over a low heat and fry the onion until deep brown. Lift the onion out and set aside.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Melt the butter with the oil over a low heat and fry the onion until deep brown. Lift the onion out and set aside.

uniqueInstructions.text: Stir the flour into the fat until well blended and cook it.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Stir the flour into the fat until well blended and cook it.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the stock a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you have a smooth, thin cream.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the stock a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you have a smooth, thin cream.

uniqueInstructions.text: Return the onion, season, and cook on, adding more stock for a thin, smooth sauce.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Return the onion, season, and cook on, adding more stock for a thin, smooth sauce.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Dried Kishk Cakes for Storing (Kishk li-l-Takhzin)
recipes.titleEn: Dried Kishk Cakes for Storing (Kishk li-l-Takhzin)

uniqueInstructions.text: Dissolve the salt in the milk.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Dissolve the salt in the milk.

uniqueInstructions.text: Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.

uniqueInstructions.text: Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.

uniqueInstructions.text: Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.

uniqueInstructions.text: Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.

uniqueInstructions.text: With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.

uniqueInstructions.text: Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.

recipes.culturalNotes: Kishk cakes keep for months. Soaked and cooked in broth, they become the cold kishk sauce served with fried onions.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Cypriot Garlic and Almond Sauce (Skordalia)

uniqueInstructions.text: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.

uniqueInstructions.text: Soak the garlic in the vinegar for 10 minutes, then add it to the bread with the almonds, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Soak the garlic in the vinegar for 10 minutes, then add it to the bread with the almonds, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat in the lemon juice and oil alternately, in thin streams, until the sauce is as thick as custard.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat in the lemon juice and oil alternately, in thin streams, until the sauce is as thick as custard.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Cypriot sauce.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

overlapAnalysis.reconciliationSummary: A recipe from Samia Abdennour’s cookbook “Egyptian Cooking”, rewritten in our own words with the source credited.

recipes.title: Turkish Hazelnut Tarator Sauce

uniqueInstructions.text: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl. Add the hazelnuts and garlic.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl. Add the hazelnuts and garlic.

uniqueInstructions.text: Beat in the vinegar, salt and oil alternately, in a thin stream, until the sauce is like a thin custard.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Beat in the vinegar, salt and oil alternately, in a thin stream, until the sauce is like a thin custard.

uniqueInstructions.text: Chill before using.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Chill before using.

uniqueInstructions.text: Hazelnuts are the original, but a mix of pine nuts, almonds and/or walnuts is also used, in which case use lemon juice instead of vinegar.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Hazelnuts are the original, but a mix of pine nuts, almonds and/or walnuts is also used, in which case use lemon juice instead of vinegar.

recipes.culturalNotes: A Turkish sauce, served with fried fish and vegetables.

source.name: Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes — Samia Abdennour (AUC Press)

recipes.title: Gulf Spiced Onion Sauce for Grilled Meat (Sharmoola)

uniqueInstructions.textEn: Lower the heat and add the onions, salt, garlic, parsley and coriander.

recipes.titleEn: Cypriot Tomato Sauce with Cinnamon and Bay (Saltsa Tomata)

uniqueInstructions.text: Fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Thin the tomato paste with an equal amount of water and add it with the sugar, bay leaf, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Thin the tomato paste with an equal amount of water and add it with the sugar, bay leaf, cinnamon, salt and pepper.

uniqueInstructions.text: Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until thick.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until thick.

uniqueInstructions.textEn: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon before using.

recipes.titleEn: Crabs Steamed with Lemon and Onion (Kaburya)

uniqueInstructions.text: Wash the crabs under running water.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Wash the crabs under running water.

uniqueInstructions.text: Put everything in a pot, without any water, over a low heat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Put everything in a pot, without any water, over a low heat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Toss from time to time; depending on their size the crabs should be done in 7–10 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Toss from time to time; depending on their size the crabs should be done in 7–10 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Eat them just as they are: crack the shells of the body and legs and pick out the meat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Eat them just as they are: crack the shells of the body and legs and pick out the meat.

uniqueInstructions.text: Wash the shrimp well and peel them.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Wash the shrimp well and peel them.

uniqueInstructions.text: Mix the flour, milk, water, egg and cumin into a thin batter.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Mix the flour, milk, water, egg and cumin into a thin batter.

uniqueInstructions.text: Dip the shrimp in the batter and deep-fry in very hot oil.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Dip the shrimp in the batter and deep-fry in very hot oil.

uniqueInstructions.textEn: Drain on absorbent paper and sprinkle with salt and cumin.

recipes.title: Egyptian Chicken Soup with Mastic and Cardamom (Shurbit Firakh)
recipes.titleEn: Egyptian Chicken Soup with Mastic and Cardamom (Shurbit Firakh)

uniqueInstructions.text: Tie the cardamom and mastic in a muslin bag.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Tie the cardamom and mastic in a muslin bag.

uniqueInstructions.text: Bring 3 cups of water to the boil with the onions and spice bag.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Bring 3 cups of water to the boil with the onions and spice bag.

uniqueInstructions.text: Lower in the chicken, season and turn down the heat.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Lower in the chicken, season and turn down the heat.

uniqueInstructions.text: When the chicken is tender, lift it out, discard the spice bag and mash the onion into the broth.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: When the chicken is tender, lift it out, discard the spice bag and mash the onion into the broth.

uniqueInstructions.text: Add the rice or vermicelli and cook for 12–15 minutes.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Add the rice or vermicelli and cook for 12–15 minutes.

uniqueInstructions.text: Palestinian version (recipe 367 in the book): just before serving, add 1–2 tablespoons of pine nuts and 1/2 cup of parsley leaves and heat without boiling.
uniqueInstructions.textEn: Palestinian version (recipe 367 in the book): just before serving, add 1–2 tablespoons of pine nuts and 1/2 cup of parsley leaves and heat without boiling.
